**Finding: Deviation (critical) — Section 13.5 Ownership**

**What I found**
- **§13.5 (p0115)** gives us ownership of "Developments" (interface coding/programs created solely by Corio to run the Software in our hosted environment), but then flips title: *"unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights."* That is an assignment of our own work product to the Vendor triggered by nothing more than a support arrangement — our walk-away position.
- **§2.8 (p0043)** Commerce One retaining the Software and all IP in it is fine and untouched; our licences in §2.1–2.3 are perpetual and irrevocable.
- **No Customer Data ownership provision** anywhere: §10 Confidentiality merely cross-refers to a separate NDA, and no clause confirms that we and our Customers retain rights in data hosted on the Corio Servers or passing through MarketSite.net.
- §13.6 (covenant not to sue) and the assignment sentence in p0116 operate in our favour, so I left them alone. The last sentence of p0116 (ownership of Software derivative works to be negotiated) is a genuinely contested area given Commerce One owns the Software, so I did not disturb it.

**Redline (validated, ok:true)**
1. Delete the ongoing-support carve-out in §13.5 so Developments created solely by Corio remain ours.
2. Add a short sentence after p0116 confirming Corio and its Customers retain all rights in Customer Data, with no assignment of Corio IP or data to Commerce One and no joint ownership.

Fallback offered in the comment: if ongoing support is the real concern, Commerce One takes a support licence to the relevant Developments rather than title.
